title: Possibility of Legislation Similar to Australia's Social Media Ban for Those Under 16 for Singapore
what_it_is: Possibility of Legislation Similar to Australia's Social Media Ban for Those Under 16 for Singapore

sections.label: Online child protection measures
sections.summary: MDDI engages Australia and has imposed age assurance on designated app stores by 31 March 2026, with plans to extend it to social media services.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Digital Development and Information)
sentences.text: The Ministry of Digital Development and Information (MDDI) is actively engaging our Australian counterparts and assessing the effectiveness of the measures in Australia.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Digital Development and Information)
sentences.text: Meanwhile, we have progressively introduced measures to better protect our children when they go online.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Digital Development and Information)
sentences.text: We have imposed age assurance requirements on designated app stores to reduce the likelihood of under-18 users accessing and downloading age-inappropriate apps of all types, beyond just social media apps.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Digital Development and Information)
sentences.text: Designated app stores are expected to implement these age assurance measures by 31 March 2026.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Digital Development and Information)
sentences.text: We also plan to extend age assurance requirements to designated social media services to reduce children's exposure to age-inappropriate content on social media platforms.

sections.label: Screen time addiction
sections.summary: Screen time is one key area and that leads to addiction.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: First is screen time, which is one key area and that leads to addiction.

sections.label: Undesirable online behaviours
sections.summary: Undesirable online behaviours include cyber bullying and behaviours the Online Safety (Relief and Accountability) Bill tries to prevent.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: The third is undesirable online behaviours, such as cyber bullying and all the types of behaviours we have tried to prevent through the Online Safety (Relief and Accountability) Bill, for example.

sections.label: Existing online safety regulations
sections.summary: Strong regulatory measures are in place, including the Code of Practice on Online Safety and age assurance requirements for apps.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: There are very strong regulatory measures that are already in place.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: We already have the Code of Practice on Online Safety for designated social media services, which we have already put in place.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: We have also implemented age assurance requirements for apps and so, it means that they now have to stop the users who are below a certain age from coming in.
